title: Industrial Designs — Registration, Copyright, Piracy and Cancellation

content.overview: The Designs Act, 2000 protects a design, meaning features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to an article by an industrial process and judged solely by the eye. Registration gives the proprietor the copyright in the design for the enacted term. Piracy is the unauthorised application of the registered design. A design is visual and applied to an article. A functional invention is a patent question.

cases.name: R.G. Anand v. Deluxe Films
cases.facts: The dispute concerned alleged copying of a dramatic work into a film.
cases.issue: What test determines substantial copyright infringement of an idea or expression.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Copyright protects expression, not ideas, and infringement depends on substantial similarity assessed from the work as a whole.
cases.holding: The Court stated the governing comparison test.
cases.relevance: Use for copyright infringement and idea-expression distinction.

cases.name: Novartis AG v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered patentability of a pharmaceutical form under s. 3(d).
cases.issue: What enhanced efficacy threshold applies to a pharmaceutical derivative.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 3(d) requires the statutory enhanced-efficacy threshold and prevents evergreening without the required proof.
cases.holding: The patent claim was rejected under the statutory standard.
cases.relevance: Use for patentability exclusions and pharmaceutical patents.

cases.name: Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
cases.facts: The parties used similar marks for pharmaceutical products.
cases.issue: How should deceptive similarity be assessed in pharmaceutical trademark disputes.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must apply a stricter likelihood-of-confusion test for medicines because confusion may endanger public health.
cases.holding: The Court directed a careful comparison of the marks and circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for trademark confusion and public-interest analysis.

enhancement.definition: The Designs Act, 2000 protects a design, meaning features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to an article by an industrial process and judged solely by the eye. Registration gives the proprietor the copyright in the design for the enacted term. Piracy is the unauthorised application of the registered design.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A design is visual and applied to an article. A functional invention is a patent question.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: A design that is a mere mechanical device or that is dictated solely by function is excluded. Registration is for a term of ten years, extendable by five as the Act enacts. Piracy includes applying the design or importing an article bearing it for sale. Cancellation lies on prior registration, prior publication or a design that should not have been registered. Copyright in an artistic work and design protection are not stacked as the Acts overlap.
enhancement.examples: A new pattern on fabric is a design. The weaving machine is a patent question. A purely functional shape is not a design.
